model_annotation: The table is a survey result showing the most feared measures that might be implemented to address the so-called "shadow economy" in a country. The horizontal bar graph lists various measures along the y-axis and their corresponding percentages along the x-axis. Each measure is represented by a different color and is marked with a percentage value to the right of the bar indicating the proportion of respondents who fear that particular measure. The results show a range of responses from lower percentages (2%) to higher percentages (13%). The most feared measure, according to the graph, is that quality control will be imposed on administrations, with 13% of respondents indicating this concern. Other measures include the imposition of anti-corruption laws, vote for ineffective stimuli for businesses, and payment of taxes in kind, all of which have been chosen fears by a significant minority of respondents, ranging from 5% to 10%. The graph is organized in descending order from the most feared measures at the top to the least feared at the bottom.
